Zoe (People Ops): Quick Q  Ben was charged a $45 late-checkout fee after a client meeting ran late. He used personal card. Is that reimbursable?

Ben (Engineering): Had to finish a post-demo debrief in the room, front desk said checkout was 2pm but meeting ended at 3:15. They charged a "late checkout" line item. I paid on my AmEx.

Priya (Finance): Generally we reimburse unavoidable hotel late checkout fees when tied to business. Need hotel folio showing the fee, manager approval, and a short note in the expense explaining why checkout was late.

Zoe (People Ops): Any threshold or reason where People Ops must approve vs manager-only?

Priya (Finance): <= $50 manager approval is sufficient. > $50 or if the fee looks like an upgrade/upsell (e.g., paid for an extra night instead of late checkout) then People Ops review required. Also watch for patterns of frequent late-checkout charges.

Ben (Engineering): The folio included a line: "Late Checkout 3:15pm $45." I also have a client meeting calendar invite showing the meeting ran over. Manager Sam said he approved in Slack.

hotel-bot: Hotel folio uploaded to expense system: folio_2090001234.pdf (shows late checkout). :pushpin:

Priya (Finance): Perfect. Ben, attach the folio, calendar invite, and paste Sam's Slack approval into the expense comments (or forward the approval email). Code as "Travel > Lodging - incidental fees". Finance will process after manager sign-off is visible.

Ben (Engineering): Will do. One more nuance: hotel tried to charge for minibar as well but I disputed it at checkout and it was removed. Only the late checkout remains.

Priya (Finance): If minibar was removed by hotel, no issue. If any disputed charges linger on the card statement, include evidence of the dispute/resolution.

Zoe (People Ops): Thanks all  I'll remind teams to request manager approval for late departures proactively next time. Closing when reimbursed.
